description: Identifying Opportunities for Climate Adaptation in the Delaware Estuary is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); Partnership for the Delaware Estuary; EPA, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. The Delaware Estuary has a nearly continuous fringe of diverse types of tidal marshes, which serve as critical habitat for fish and wildlife and provide important services for residents in the surrounding area. Much of this habitat is presently stressed by human alterations and activities and climate change impacts appear to be exacerbating these issues. Coverage: Wilmington, DE (2008). The toolkit gives Wilmington, DE as the location, 2008 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
